shared_elements: carved stone monument displayed in a museum
incised low-relief linear detail on a rough stone surface
head with defined brow and facial features
justification: Both are weathered stone sculptures of anthropomorphic subjects with shallow incised detail (linear hatching on A's headdress/limbs, circular and banded motifs on B's body), and both show a defined head above a broader body mass. The decisive difference is form: A is a fully three-dimensional, deeply undercut figure in a crouched, twisting pose in pale stone, while B is a flat-fronted, slab-like dark monolith whose imagery is confined to a single frontal relief plane.
